bindings.label: thm:lower_boundary_mu_half
bindings.note: The checked parameter range is 0≤mu≤2, as in the preceding definition of the relaxed profile. The printed KKT proof route is not certified here.

bindings.label: thm:final_explicit_region
bindings.note: The lower estimate is checked for nonpositive footrule with the unique parameter restricted to [0,2]. The unrestricted real-root uniqueness sentence is false and refuted separately.

bindings.quote: the parameter $\mu(y)$ is the unique real solution
bindings.note: At y=-1/2 there are two distinct real roots, 2 and -1. Only the admissible root in [0,2] is unique for y in [-1/2,0].

bindings.label: eq:two_param_copula_density
bindings.note: The measure identity is checked on the full closed parameter square. Density values on null fibers are immaterial; no pointwise division by a zero marginal density is claimed.

sourceDiscrepancies.unverified_claim: The printed 3-by-3 checkerboard matrix is LTD.
sourceDiscrepancies.evidence: Lean proves its CDF at (2/3, 2/3) is 5/12, below 4/9, so the matrix is not LTD.
sourceDiscrepancies.verified_instead: The corrected matrix printed in final JCAM Remark 2(d) is proved LTD with xi=38/81 and footrule=10/27.

sourceDiscrepancies.unverified_claim: The cubic has a unique real solution mu(y).
sourceDiscrepancies.evidence: At y=-1/2, both mu=2 and mu=-1 are distinct real roots; Lean proves footrule_cubic_not_unique_real.

verificationScope: The original arXiv v1 text, title date, formulas, result numbers, proofs, figures, tables and bibliography are retained. The xi and footrule definitions, Frechet CDF and complete Theorem 2.1 maximum/attainment/uniqueness statement have independent typed encodings and checked correspondences. Other links expose actual compiled counterparts and their precise hypotheses. The false LTD example hypothesis and unrestricted real-root uniqueness are visibly refuted, with checked corrections. The original KKT proofs, the external copula-characterization lemma, Appendix Lemmas A.1–A.2, every printed intermediate proof claim, and numerical table/figure claims are not yet certified. A compiled alternative proof of a conclusion does not certify its printed argument.
